column3: Manifest for the shared boot glue: version 0.2.1-rc.2, a separate ./worker/profile-resolution-bootstrap export, deps ajv/regexpp/semver/js-yaml plus workspace peers for the cordis loader, group and include plugins.
Per-heading en/zh content hashes for README.md's bilingual-pairing check; 22 heading sections recorded with the command that re-records them.

Full package doc: the two-call boot entry point, the global required-plugin list (agent-loop, webserver, web-runtime, modules, connection, headless-runner, acp, sdk-jsonrpc-server), and the profile/compatibility/exemption rules.
Chinese mirror of README.md; I read the English in full and this file's first 60 lines, which carry the same boot, required-list and exemption narrative.

Preflight that denies an incompatible plugin by rewriting only the LAUNCHER's composition: ordinary rows gain disabled:true, a native Include reaching a denied plugin is dropped whole, and the user's patch/manifest/bundle list are never touched.

Boot-free discovery of plugin Config schemas: walks the composed entry list and Include descendants through the profile's module resolution, treating malformed rows as positioned diagnostics instead of losing siblings.

Builds the final JSON Schema document: entry/patch structure, collected plugin schemas, and an x-cordis block whose complete flag is false for any error diagnostic, partial/unsupported/error entry, or ambiguous plugin name.
Public entry for generateConfigSchema: turns skipped bundles into error diagnostics, composes patch layers, creates the runtime resolution, and delegates to the collector.
Identity check for the native Schemastery graph: requires the Symbol.for('schemastery') marker plus a string type and an object meta, so a schema is inspected without invoking a validator.

Regex portability checker using regexpp: a pattern may only be emitted as a JSON Schema constraint when its AST is identical under Unicode and non-Unicode semantics (BMP-only, no broad set that could observe a surrogate midpoint).

Projects native Config input constraints into JSON Schema without executing validators or transforms; tracks acceptsMissing, effectful (transform callbacks) and mutating (native resolution writes values) flags and records limitations instead of inventing defaults.
Type definitions for the JSON Schema 2020-12 output, the x-cordis annotation block, the native Schemastery graph shape, and the collected-entry record.

The boot library core: env layering, fail-loud guards, snapshot-aware config path resolution, patch composition, the Loader boot sequence, and the required-versus-optional startup audit with its diagnostic renderers.
Two-line constant listing the on-demand installable bundles (dsh-subagent-claude-code, dsh-subagent-codex); the single source for both offline catalog generation and release ordering.
Generated offline catalog with localized title/description and a base64 SVG icon per official bundle; header says it is produced by pnpm gen-official-bundle-catalog and must not be edited.
Declares the OfficialBundleCatalogEntry shape (exact npm package name plus package-owned localized text and icon) and re-exports the generated catalog.

Reads plugin display text and icons through exported resources without evaluating plugin code; icon paths must be relative and stay inside the manifest directory or package directory, are capped at 256 KiB, and only SVG/PNG/JPEG/WebP are admitted.

Evaluates a plugin's dsh requirements without importing it: engines.dsh decides alone and peerDependencies are ignored when it is present, otherwise every @deepseek-ai/dsh* peer must match; prereleases count, workspace: peers mean the current runtime, and empty/invalid ranges are unmet.

Profile-local compatibility.json: maps exact package-name@version keys to exact DSH runtime versions, reads defensively (a bad file grants nothing and is reported, never fatal) and refuses to rewrite a file it rejected.

Launcher-owned profile facts (dir, patch path, install anchor, home, overlays, telemetry opt-out) plus the rule that ANY non-empty DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED value disables telemetry, including '0' and 'false'.
Reads installed profile dependencies and reconciles bundle activation after a package-manager operation, keeping template entries' order and duplicates and auto-activating newly installed bundles.

Canonicalizes module paths through the active carrier's filesystem: realpathSync.native outside a packaged executable, and a symlink-preserving variant inside one where SEA archive files are symlink-free.

In-memory package routing for Node's ESM and CommonJS resolvers: an interception layer that answers entries from the declaring manifest, with four explicit routes and a replaceable generation so a running process can publish a new resolution.
The pluginPackages service: owns the runtime interception, publishes the resolution to Workers through worker_threads environment data, and caches parsed manifests per (dir, name).
Twelve-line Worker entry that installs the inherited runtime resolution from worker_threads environment data, and does nothing when no data was inherited.
Profile recovery for a broken profile: renames the patch file to a timestamped backup (with a collision ordinal) and rewrites only the bundle list, without parsing the broken patch.

Profile discovery, init, manifest round-trips, two-anchor bundle resolution and patch-layer composition; composeEntries uses the same applyEntryPatches call the boot include makes, so a config dump equals what mounts.

Tests for config-path resolution (including snapshot replay), .env loading, fail-loud behavior, and the required/optional startup audit, including nested AggregateError causes and circular cause chains.
Tests that an incompatible plugin is blocked before import, that an exempted pair is allowed, and that a denied native Include is omitted as a whole; records plugin import/apply effects to a file.

Tests that the offline config dump parses back to exactly what boot() mounts, prints !!js verbatim, labels each section with its source and the layers that changed it, and warns (not fails) for a patch whose target is absent.

Table-driven expectations for which regexes survive Unicode/native semantics; rejects a negated broad set, a lookaround, and any pattern with a surrogate range, and does not hide an unexpected parser failure.
Tests Include refresh against an invalid or empty file (keeps the last good tree instead of throwing) and that overlay patches are re-applied on every re-read, with parity to the initial load.

Tests the generated schema document end to end with a real Schemastery schema and Ajv 2020, including skipped-bundle diagnostics, partial entries and the release of the interception when the Node module loader is unavailable.
Helper that rethrows Node resolver errors with a writable 'stack' property, matching what an asynchronous module.register() hook chain returns to the main thread.

Differential matrix comparing native Node lookup against the profile's projected lookup across 3 layouts, 7 methods, 4 importer positions and 6 package sources; every case must agree with the native observation.
Detects the running Node loader's internal shape (v1 vs v2) because 24.0-24.11.1 report major 24 while carrying v1; a tag taken from the Node major rejects every call.
Tests that the offline catalog holds exactly the two native subagent integrations, each with both shipped languages and a base64 SVG icon, and carries no version field.
Tests that plugin locale metadata resolves without executing the plugin, that file-address specifiers are refused, and that icons must stay inside their package directory.
Table-driven tests for engines.dsh vs peerDependencies precedence, prerelease inclusion, workspace: peer handling, and the exact text of the compatibility warning.
Tests that a malformed compatibility.json grants nothing but never blocks the profile, that grants persist with 0600 mode, and that a grant left by an older runtime can still be revoked.
Tests the dependency inventory (alias keys, installed versions, loader precedence) and the bundle reconciliation, including that a second reconciliation writes nothing.
Tests that the pluginPackages service refreshes from the profile and installation, replaces a resolution generation, and republishes it to Worker environment data.

Differential tests for the runtime resolution over ESM and CommonJS: package imports, subpath fallthrough, null exports, conditional exports, native require stacks, and the linked-root peer projections.
Mocks worker_threads and the resolver to assert the Worker bootstrap installs only the inherited resolution and does nothing when none was inherited.
Tests profile recovery: the patch is backed up with a timestamped name (collisions get an ordinal), a broken plugin manifest is left alone, and a backup failure happens before any activation change.
Tests profile directory resolution and init, manifest round-trips, two-anchor bundle resolution, patch-layer loading, empty-root composition and the runtime package table.

Tests the JSON Schema projection against Ajv: omission/null acceptance, required derived from fallback validation rather than meta.required, anyOf (not oneOf) for overlapping unions, and callbacks never executed.

Tests the optional patch-list loader (!!js expressions preserved as loader expression nodes, absolute plugin paths converted to file URLs) and that boot() applies the user layer over a real Loader tree.
TypeScript project file: src to lib/types, referencing the vendored cordis, loader, include and group plus the launch-environment, home-paths, package-manifest and atomic-write utilities.
Build config that bundles cordis-plugin-include into the output while keeping Loader external, so the built include tree and the app host bind to one Loader peer.
Manifest for the command-line handoff package; commander is a devDependency only, so the package never ships a parser.
Per-heading en/zh hashes for the cmdline README's bilingual pairing, 20 heading sections.
Doc for the immutable launcher-to-app handoff: cmdlineArgs, appExit and appReady, the rule that a flag beats a config value, and the note that reading never consumes the arguments.
Chinese mirror of the cmdline README; I read the English in full and this file's first 30 lines, which carry the same launcher-value and flag-precedence narrative.

Provides cmdlineArgs/appExit/appReady as services and adapts commander to the launcher, including a structural isCommanderError check because an out-of-tree commander copy is a different class identity.

Tests the handoff over a real Loader tree: flags resolve into a consumer's config through injection ordering, --help exits 0 without starting the consumer, and stdin EOF binds to a bounded exit only after readiness.
TypeScript project file for cmdline, referencing the vendored cordis, include and loader projects.
English locale stub for the config-editor plugin: a meta.title only.
Chinese locale for the config-editor plugin: title and a one-line description.
Manifest for the config editor; dsh-hmr is an OPTIONAL peer, so the editor works without HMR (it then runs its own reconciliation directly).
Per-heading en/zh hashes for the config-editor README's bilingual pairing, 13 sections.
Doc for the config editor: writes validate the complete candidate before touching disk, serialize with profile changes and HMR, and invalid values or higher-layer overrides leave the file unchanged.
Chinese mirror of the config-editor README; I read the English in full and this file's first 25 lines.

Persists plugin configuration through the profile patch: composes inherited and override values, edits the YAML document preserving comments and !!js expressions, and rolls back the document and the Loader patches if reconciliation fails.
TypeScript project file for the config editor, referencing cordis, loader, the hmr and app-boot projects and the atomic-write utility.
MIT license text, copyright Shigma.
English locale stub for the hmr plugin: a meta.title only.
Chinese locale for the hmr plugin: title and a one-line description of reloading plugin code and configuration at runtime.
Manifest for the hmr package; deps chokidar 5.0.0, babel/code-frame and picomatch, and peers the cordis timer, loader and include plugins.
Per-heading en/zh hashes for the hmr README's bilingual pairing, 20 sections including a KV-cache subsection.

Doc for the coordinated reload queue, the config table (base/root/ignored/debounce), the awaitWriteFinish default, and the rule that a failed replacement is reported as failed rather than as a restart.
Chinese mirror of the hmr README; I read the English in full and this file's first 30 lines, which cover the base bundle's root:[] default.
Formats esbuild build failures with babel code frames when a source location is available, and forwards any unrecognized error to the logger unchanged.
The reload engine: module graph analysis, accepted/declined dependency sets, partial reload with rollback, one exclusive queue for every reload, and the profile/package replacement path.

Tracks disk identity (inode, size, mtime) of loaded modules to find stale ones; deliberately does not record change time because a hard link changes it without changing content, and reads the OS clock from a marker file's mtime.
Expires Node's cached package configuration by patching the native modules binding and the package_json_reader, restoring each method only while its replacement is still installed.

Watches exactly one patch file (never siblings), finds the nearest existing ancestor as the root with a depth limit, defaults to awaitWriteFinish, and re-attaches an error listener across close so Windows EPERM cannot become an uncaught exception.
Tests the exclusive queue: nesting is refused, the queue survives a failure, config handlers wait behind config mutations, and a provider reconfiguration rebinds its watchers.
Tests that an unrecognized error is forwarded without being dropped and that compiler source locations are formatted, including a vanished source file.
Standalone fixture that invalidates the filesystem-root package.json and asserts Node's scope and nearest-manifest lookups are unchanged; reads but never modifies the root.
Tests that the file clock is read from a marker file that is removed again, and that an unwritable temp directory falls back to the system clock.

Tests the module graph replacement over a controlled loader: a runtime removed during dependency traversal is not reactivated, and a failed replacement reports the ORIGINAL error when restoring the old plugin also fails.
Tests that a package.json change dispatches a plugin replacement through a real Loader, deduplicating the replacement when the module namespace is unchanged.

Tests that an invalidated manifest is re-read by Node's resolver, that filename-based resolve hooks and node-prefixed builtins survive invalidation, and that dispose restores only the methods it replaced.

Tests that profile reconciliation replaces plugins whose installed files changed, that a module first loaded during a recomposition whose file changed is replaced, and that an unreplaceable plugin is reported as pending rather than failing the whole reload.
Tests that profile watches wait for application readiness before applying, and that a patch edited after boot parsing but before watcher registration is still applied.
Tests Include recomposition after each delivered file event: a failed candidate is reported, an invalid disabled expression and a parse failure are reported, and a later valid edit recovers.
Tests exact-path watching, including the darwin FSEvents start-up race workaround (a directory open/close forces the stream to arm) and the path-resolution error branches.
TypeScript project file for hmr, referencing the vendored cordis, loader, include, timer and schemastery plus app-boot and cmdline.
English locale stub for the plugin-manager plugin: a meta.title only.
English locale stub for the plugin-manager TOOLS entry point: a meta.title only.
Chinese locale for the plugin-manager tools entry point: a meta.title only.
Chinese locale for the plugin-manager plugin: title and a one-line description of managing plugins in the current configuration.
Manifest for the plugin manager, exporting ./types, ./registry, ./tools, ./typert and ./remote subpaths; dsh-hmr and dsh-user-approval are OPTIONAL peers.
Per-heading en/zh hashes for the plugin-manager README's bilingual pairing, 21 sections.

Doc for the plugin manager, including the rule that the profile patch records only DEPARTURES from the bundles, the failure-behavior table (what survives a failed install/enable/remove), and that pnpm's zero exit code does not mean publication succeeded.
Chinese mirror of the plugin-manager README; I read the English in full and this file's first 20 lines.

Records pnpm's ignored build scripts into pnpm-workspace.yaml allowBuilds using pnpm's own placeholder string, and approves only named pending packages atomically; YAML anchors and aliases are refused because a shared node would change another package's permission.
Defines the ManagementFailure error carrying a localizable code plus the incompatible package list, and the helper that drops the exemption status from an unexempted compatibility result.
Read-only pre-flight GitHub reachability check with credential helpers disabled, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT off, a timeout that kills descendants, and a bounded tail read from a 0600 log file.
The plugin manager service: list/enable/remove bundles and plugins, install with registry failover, version exemptions, and the disk-state fingerprint used to decide whether a change actually landed.

Classifies a failed pnpm run by how it ended first (timeout, pnpm missing) and then by the most specific stable code in its output; the table is ordered so a specific code precedes the generic network family.
Reads an install spec into registry/path/tarball/git form, refuses relative local paths and names a registry would refuse, and rebuilds the spec pnpm accepts for an already-recorded dependency.

Chooses the install target for an official bundle: a link: to the workspace package for a source checkout, an exact published version otherwise, and a hard error (never a registry fallback) for an incomplete checkout.

The shared profile package operations: runs pnpm with a scrubbed environment, bounds the captured output and the idle time, writes a log file, and checks installed packages for dsh requirement violations after the run.

Comment-preserving enablement edits: writes only disabled into the last matching override and removes the override entirely when the bundle layers already imply the requested state, keeping anchors other entries reference.

Plans the registries one operation asks, in order: pnpm's own registry joins the fallback set only when it is known to be public, a private or unknown default is asked ALONE, and a failure is attributed to the registry or to the spec's own host by reading error lines only.
Waits for a terminated run's whole process tree to disappear (POSIX process group or the process itself) before the caller unlocks the profile, with a 5 s bound and injectable liveness probes.
Agent-facing plugin_manager tool: maps every refusal code and package failure kind to one sentence telling the model what to do next, and a refusal code beats a failure kind.
Public record types: the read-only reasons, the management error codes, the restart reasons (no-hmr, package-moved, host-module, unmanaged-plugin, module-comparison), and the event vocabulary.
Tests that pending script permissions survive a cleanup, that an unlisted approval is rejected atomically, and that pnpm file-dependency selectors are preserved verbatim.

Helper that removes Git's indexed command-line configuration group from the test process environment, because the shared scrub would strip the counter but not its key and the child would fail before reading any config file.
Tests the bounded Git check against a local proxy: a reachable repository passes, a timeout kills the descendants, and a credential prompt is never triggered.
Table-driven tests for every accepted spec form and every refusal reason, plus the failure classification including that 401/403/404 responses are left out of connection recovery.

The manager's behavioural suite over a real profile Include and Loader: restore-on-failure, refusal before running pnpm, registry failover with per-registry progress events, and version-exemption matching against the actual alias manifest.
Tests that a source checkout yields a link: target found by manifest name, and that a missing, duplicated, private or unbuilt workspace package is refused without a registry fallback.
Tests that the pnpm log file descriptor is released when the profile manifest cannot be parsed, so no file handle leaks on the failure path.
Tests the bounded drain and the tree stop against real child processes: a descendant outliving its parent is killed, and a silent child is ended by the idle bound.

Tests the CLI/service package operations: path anchoring, the pre-install pnpm view lookup, incompatible installed packages failing the run, and the manifest restored after a malformed installed peer metadata.

Tests GUI package operations around activation and disposal: a shared dependency survives the removal of its first declaring bundle, and a reinstallation that cannot compare loaded module files reports restart-required with reason module-comparison.
Tests the enablement edits preserve comments, !!js expressions and unrelated configuration, are idempotent, and keep a switch whose anchor or alias other entries reference.
Pure table-driven tests for the registry plan (including that a private pnpm registry is never a fallback for a public mirror) and for failure attribution to the registry or the spec host.
Tests group leadership per execution mode and platform, and that a tree which never disappears ends at the wait bound without fake timers.

Tests the agent tool denies every management action in read-only and workspace-write modes BEFORE touching the manager, preserves bundle load errors, and produces the documented next-step text per outcome.
TypeScript project file for the plugin manager, referencing 19 sibling projects (agent, tools, sandbox, approvals, typert protocol and others).
Manifest for the plugin market reader, exporting ./types, ./tools, ./typert and ./remote; the settings peer is OPTIONAL.
Per-heading en/zh hashes for the plugin-market README's bilingual pairing, 18 sections.

Doc for the market reader: no index source is configured by default, only a configured URL is ever fetched, and the measured limits (20k plugins ~0.8 s build, ~130 MiB heap; a 38 MiB index blocks the Host event loop ~190 ms during clone).
Chinese mirror of the plugin-market README; I read the English in full and this file's first 20 lines.
Validates and normalizes an index source URL: http(s) only, no credentials, no fragment, reported with a machine-readable reason.

The market service: fetches configured indexes with a deadline and a byte cap, caches them, parses them in a Worker, and annotates every entry with the profile's installation status and dsh compatibility.
Runs the index parse in a fresh Worker Thread with the body buffer transferred, and settles on the first message, an error, an exit without a result, or an abort, always terminating the Worker.
Decodes a body as strict UTF-8, parses it as JSON and validates it as format 1, returning the first violation's JSON path, rule and message.

Fuzzy search over one index: NFKC normalization, CJK runs split into overlapping character pairs so a query matches without word segmentation, fuzzy distance capped at 2, and a MiniSearch index built in chunks.
Read-only plugin_market agent tool: paged listings, a 300-character cap on market-supplied text, and the tool registered only while the pluginMarket service is mounted.
Record types for the market's Remote namespace, the RemoteErrorDetailsMap with one machine-readable reason per failure, and the installation/compatibility statuses.
Seven-line Worker entry that validates its workerData shape and posts the parse result back to its parent.
Built-artifact guard: runs the published lib/index.js under plain node so the bundled lib/worker.cjs is exercised with no workspace packages; skipped until a build produces both artifacts.
Tests that index sources persist through the profile patch and Settings, that the service is NOT remounted (the same fiber survives), and that the list is restored at restart.
Fixture patch inserting the config-editor, settings, plugin-manager and plugin-market rows with one configured index URL.
Tests that a parse Worker crash surfaces as plugin-market/fetch-failed with the crash reason, not as an invalid-index error.
Tests the market service: fetch refusals, caching and page pinning by fetchedAt, installation and compatibility annotation, and CJK/full-width/decomposed text normalization against the search index.
Tests the Worker lifecycle with a scripted Worker: the body is transferred, the first message wins, termination failure still settles, and an unexpected message is refused.
Runs the source-mode parse Worker end to end and asserts the body buffer is consumed (zero length afterwards) and a malformed body yields a path diagnostic.
Tests the body parser: relative icons resolve against the index URL, and malformed UTF-8, malformed JSON and a format violation each report a path and a reason.
Tests the read-only listing tool over the same service the Discover page uses, including that the tool disappears when the pluginMarket service is disposed.
TypeScript project file for the plugin market, referencing cordis, loader, schemastery, app-boot, plugin-manager, the market-index utility, settings, the typert protocol and core/tools.
Build config that emits the service as ESM and the parse Worker as a separate CJS bundle carrying its whole closure, because the Worker starts without the parent's profile resolver.
Per-heading en/zh hashes for the boot group README's bilingual pairing, 7 sections.
Group doc mapping the six boot packages to their ctx keys (cmdlineArgs, appExit, hmr, configEditor, pluginManager, pluginMarket).
Chinese mirror of the boot group README; I read the English in full and this file's first 30 lines, which carry the same package table.
The ACP bundle patch: sets the coding-agent persona, disables session titles and HMR, and inserts the startup provider plus the ACP row that injects acpAppStartup.
Manifest for the ACP bundle, declaring dsh.bundle.patch ./cordis.patch.yml and depending on dsh-acp, dsh-cmdline and commander.
Per-heading en/zh hashes for the acp-app README's bilingual pairing, 19 sections.
Doc for the ACP profile: stdout belongs to ACP, the bridge starts only after the startup provider accepts the invocation, and configuration changes require a restart because the bundle disables HMR.
Chinese mirror of the acp-app README; I read the English in full and this file's first 15 lines.
The ACP startup provider: a zero-option commander program whose action binds stdin EOF to the launcher's bounded exit and publishes acpAppStartup, so --help starts no transport.
Tests the bundle's declared patch: HMR and session titles disabled, and the acp row injecting acpAppStartup with the shipped provider and model.
Tests the startup provider publishes readiness and requests a bounded exit on EOF, and that --help prints help without publishing readiness or binding stdin.
TypeScript project file for the ACP bundle, referencing cordis and the cmdline package.

The shared core's single insert over the empty profile root: ~100 rows covering LLM, session, agents, tools, sandboxes, compaction, subagents and the DeepSeek adapter; each row's config is owned wholly by one layer.
Manifest for the base bundle, declaring dsh.bundle.patch ./cordis.patch.yml and ~100 workspace dependencies that ARE the shipped core plugin set.
Per-heading en/zh hashes for the base bundle README's bilingual pairing, 21 sections.

Doc for the shared core: what a base-backed profile provides (model access, full tool set, durable sessions, safety defaults), the OTel FEEDBACK_ONLY default, and the rule that a mode-specific default lives in that surface's bundle.
Chinese mirror of the base bundle README; I read the English in full and this file's first 15 lines.
Nine-line module with no runtime API; the bundle's substance is its cordis.patch.yml.

Tests the base patch parses, inserts over 50 rows, carries the telemetry and HMR defaults, excludes the on-demand subagent bundles, and gates each shell stack with a symmetric platform expression evaluated on every host.
One-line fixture: an empty root entry list.
TypeScript project file for the base bundle, referencing cordis, the config-editor and the settings project.

The one-shot bundle patch: persona, the PTC tools mode env seam, the headless startup provider and runner rows, HMR disabled, and the managed credential store, authorization and DeepSeek account rows disabled.
Manifest for the headless bundle, declaring the bundle patch and a ./startup export; dsh-subagent is an OPTIONAL peer.
Per-heading en/zh hashes for the headless README's bilingual pairing, 26 sections.

Doc for one-shot mode: exit codes, the credential chain (launch env, then cwd .env, then $DSH_HOME/.env), the cwd/ownership/preset-scoped rules for --session-id adoption, and that the JSON stream is a projection rather than the log.
Chinese mirror of the headless README; I read the English in full and this file's first 15 lines.

The one-shot runner: creates or adopts one Agent through the core registry, drives it to quiescence, streams provider reasoning to stderr, prints the final answer and maps the turn outcome to an exit code.
The --json projection: every event is a commit point taken from committed assistant/message content, with an 8 KiB per-string cap, a depth cap of 64 and an untruncated terminal final.
Process streams the runner reads and writes, kept out of the package entry so substituting them in tests adds no public API.
Process facts the startup provider reads (isTTY, stdout), likewise kept out of the public entry.
The one-shot command-line provider: parses the task positional, --session-id and --json, and in JSON mode overrides commander's error printer so a grammar error still owes the caller an error event.
A read-only POSIX filesystem fixture provider with its own execution coordinates, so host and provider paths never coincide.

Tests the one-shot driver: durable summary, exit-code mapping, the error text, reading the task from stdin, exact Session adoption with its refusal rules, and that the runner fails loud without the launcher exit request.
Tests the projection's commit-point emission, ordering, foreign-session rejection, disposal, and the bounded line writer.
Tests the one-shot command provider over a real Loader tree: the task and options reach the runner's config, help leaves the runner pending, and an interactive stdin with no task is a usage error.
Tests exit status when a parent summary cannot commit: one agent/error, exit 1, an error event instead of a final in JSON mode, and that another Agent's failure is ignored.
TypeScript project file for the headless bundle, referencing cordis, loader, schemastery, agent, agent-default-model, llm, session, cmdline, session-query, fs and subagent.
Per-heading en/zh hashes for the bundle group README's bilingual pairing, 7 sections.
Group doc mapping the six profile bundles to their roles, and noting that in-box bundles resolve from the installation while out-of-tree bundles install into a profile.
Chinese mirror of the bundle group README; I read the English in full and this file's first 15 lines.

The SDK bundle patch: persona, session titles and HMR disabled, the startup provider and JSON-RPC server rows, and workspace-dependency and Office-skill rows gated on the packaged primary runtime environment.
Manifest for the SDK bundle, declaring the bundle patch and depending on the SDK server, cmdline, schemastery, commander, the Office skill and the workspace-dependency tool.
Per-heading en/zh hashes for the sdk-app README's bilingual pairing, 15 sections.
Doc for the SDK profile: stdout belongs to JSON-RPC, DSH_MAX_TOKENS_AS_SUCCESS decides whether a token-limited subagent completion is accepted, and the tool roster omits str_replace_editor.
Chinese mirror of the sdk-app README; I read the English in full and this file's first 15 lines.
The SDK startup provider: a zero-option commander program whose action binds stdin EOF and publishes sdkAppStartup, with the profile name rendered in the help grammar.
Tests the bundle's declared patch, including that the JSON-RPC row injects both sdkAppStartup and loader.
Tests the SDK startup provider: readiness plus a bounded exit on EOF, help that starts no transport, and the selected profile name rendered in help.
TypeScript project file for the SDK bundle, referencing cordis, schemastery and the cmdline package.

The standalone minimal profile's COMPLETE tree in one insert: 35 rows with no base bundle, explicit shell stack per platform, file tools reduced to read_image, danger-full-access policy and uncompressed JSONL sessions.
Manifest for the standalone minimal bundle: its dependencies are exactly the packages its rows name, which a test enforces.
Per-heading en/zh hashes for the sdk-minimal README's bilingual pairing, 18 sections.
Doc for the standalone minimal profile: what it excludes (base, Web, settings, credentials, telemetry, text file tools, skills, jobs, subagents) and the danger-full-access warning about the shell.
Chinese mirror of the sdk-minimal README; I read the English in full and this file's first 15 lines.
Nine-line module with no runtime interface; the bundle's substance is its cordis.patch.yml.
Tests the exact ordered row list, the environment-backed defaults and that the manifest dependencies equal the set of packages the rows name.
TypeScript project file for the minimal bundle, referencing only the vendored cordis project.

The browser-surface patch: restates the base's surface-specific values (persona, session-query-sqlite, tools mode), inserts the web host rows and browser roster, disables the base's per-agent tool rows in favour of presets, and mounts the preset registry.
English locale stub for the web-app bundle: a meta.title only.
English locale stub for the web-app/startup entry: a meta.title only.
Chinese locale for the web-app/startup entry: a meta.title only.
Chinese locale for the web-app bundle: title and a one-line description.
Manifest for the web bundle; dsh.bundle.patch lists FIVE files (the web patch plus the four preset patches) and the dependencies are the whole browser roster.
The cordis agent preset: one dsh-agent-preset declaration with an ordered plugin list including a plan-mode group and a compaction group with a tool-result pruner.
The minimal agent preset: a fixed persona, file tools reduced to read_image, a compaction group and a platform-selected persistent shell group.
The ptc agent preset: the standard roster plus the PTC tool-presentation row, with the workflow rows disabled.
The standard agent preset: the shipped default (order 1) with persona, instructions, shell tools, file tools, plan mode, compaction, delegation, ask-user, todo and web.
Per-heading en/zh hashes for the web-app README's bilingual pairing, 28 sections.
